caps.text: A bid is a promise.
Most bids cost nothing. A film by Harsh Bhanushali and Dhairya Patel.
GAVEL. Every bid is a hold. The hammer is the payment.
Charge a card up front, and bidders hold back.
Leave bids unsecured, and winners walk away.
Shout bids on paper, and the record is hard to trust.
Authorize a ceiling.
Bid under it.
Capture only the winner.
Release the rest. Orders v2 intent AUTHORIZE; Payments v2 capture with final_capture, void.
A judge opens /try. One tap, one sandbox room.
A join code and a ticket QR.
A bidder types the code. Or scans the ticket QR.
Pick a ceiling. The most this bidder may bid.
Hold the button 3 seconds.
Held, not charged.
The auctioneer opens the lot.
Bids arrive from the phones.
Prices only go up.
Every screen agrees.
Or say it.
"three fifty for paddle twelve"
amount 350.00, paddle 12
Did you mean $350 for paddle 12? Confirm. Illustration: speech is measured on 24 synthetic clips only (G5 partial).
Hold the hammer 3 seconds. No accidental sales.
Sold.
The big screen names the winner.
Capture only the winning price.
Release every other hold. Drawn, not recorded: real sandbox capture and void are proven in G1 and G4.
A receipt for every bidder.
With a share link and a QR.
Paste a ledger export.
Chain verified. Then one entry is edited.
Chain broken.
Kill survived. A real server kill during settlement, on the PayPal sandbox: one capture, two holds voided, a ledger of 19 entries that verifies.
Live voice 24 of 24. Both speech providers answered 24 of 24 synthetic clips through the live socket. No bid accepted without a confirm.
Webhooks 6 of 6. Six real PayPal sandbox deliveries verified SUCCESS against the webhook id.
Latency, honestly. Hammer to captured p95 3.8 s against a 2.5 s target. Hammer to settled p95 6.9 s against 6 s. Both missed.
For judges. One shared judge key, in the Devpost testing instructions. It opens sandbox rooms over plain HTTP and nothing else. No key is needed for /try.
The key goes into a password field on /try. The docs list every call with a Try-it panel.
